jurisdiction.name: Hungary
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: In 2025 Hungary replaced its 2020 innovation-led AI strategy with a renewed AI strategy for 2025-2030, appointed a Government Commissioner for AI and adopted a series of government resolutions requiring AI commissioners in every ministry, a public-administration AI strategy and a sandbox proposal. Act LXXV of 2025 and Government Decree 344/2025 implement the EU AI Act, naming the National Accreditation Authority as notifying authority, the minister for enterprise development as market surveillance authority and single point of contact, and creating a Hungarian AI Council. The data protection authority (NAIH) is the most active AI regulator, including a 2022 fine on a bank for AI emotion analysis of call recordings and a 2025 report on banks' AI systems.
lead_institutions: National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (NAIH)
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. All records were read on official sources; the AI Council's outputs and a sandbox decree were not yet published and are listed as leads.

instruments.summary: Government resolution calling on every minister to appoint AI commissioners in the ministries, on county government offices to appoint AI officers, and on universities and research institutes to appoint AI experts (deadline 31 March 2026). It tasks the Minister for Public Administration with a comprehensive strategy for AI use across state administration covering risk and impact assessment, ethical controls and training, the AI Government Commissioner with an implementation framework for the national AI strategy, a proposal on industrial testing environments (sandboxes) with regulatory exemptions, and the conditions for the Hungarian AI Council, and the Interior Minister with a health-sector AI report and strategy.

instruments.current_status: Adopted 21 October 2025, promulgated 31 October 2025; in force from the 31st day after promulgation (1 December 2025), with the sandbox provisions (s. 3(2) and s. 10) applying from 2 August 2026.
instruments.summary: Hungary's AI Act implementing law: it empowers the Government to designate by decree the AI notifying authority (Art. 28) and the AI market surveillance authority (Art. 70), sets their procedures, fines and powers (excluding high-risk systems of MNB-supervised financial institutions from the general authority), and requires the market surveillance authority to run an AI regulatory sandbox from 2 August 2026. It establishes the Hungarian Artificial Intelligence Council, chaired by the Government Commissioner for AI and including NMHH, MNB, GVH, NAIH, SZTFH, the IP office and the tax authority, to issue recommendations and guidelines, coordinate AI Act implementation and draft and review the national AI strategy and a public-sector sub-strategy.

instruments.current_status: Promulgated 26 July 2011; main provisions in force since 1 January 2012; amended many times (consolidated text read 2026-10-12).
instruments.summary: Hungary's general data protection and freedom of information act (Infotv.), supplementing the GDPR and governing processing outside its scope (e.g. law enforcement, national security). Section 6 permits decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, with adverse or significant effects only where authorised by law or EU law and with safeguards; it also establishes NAIH as the supervisory authority.

instruments.summary: NAIH inquiry report, signed by President Attila Péterfalvi, on how three Hungarian banks use AI systems that process personal data: image processing, text processing, training data, "shadow AI" use by staff, creditworthiness and product-affinity scoring, and anonymisation. It sets out the national AI Act implementation framework and the authority's data-protection expectations for banks' AI use, recalling its earlier NAIH-85-3/2022 fine.

instruments.english_title: NAIH Decision NAIH-85-3/2022 (data protection issues of the use of artificial intelligence)
instruments.issuing_authority: Hungarian National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (NAIH)
instruments.current_status: Decision dated 8 February 2022 (Budapest); published on naih.hu under the title "Mesterséges intelligencia alkalmazásának adatvédelmi kérdései".
instruments.summary: Ex officio decision against Budapest Bank Zrt. finding that its AI-driven speech analysis of customer-service call recordings, which assessed callers' emotions to prioritise call-backs, breached GDPR principles, legal basis, transparency, the right to object and data protection by design. NAIH ordered the bank to stop analysing emotions and fined it HUF 250 million.
